st: The Case of the Counterfeit Crank
d: An old man is betrayed by his nephew after he alters his company's books to divert attention from the young man.

st: The Case of the Ancient Romeo
d: Perry Mason gets a client accused of murder when the dueling scene in a production of "Romeo and Juliet" takes on a sudden reality.

st: The Case of the Promoter's Pillbox
d: A young pharmacist who wants to be a television writer stumbles over a dead body and is accused of murder.

st: The Case of the Lonely Eloper
d: An immature young woman is the prime suspect when her domineering legal guardian is found murdered.

st: The Case of the Bogus Books
d: A thriving racket in first-edition books comes to light after a bookstore proprietor is found slain in a locked room.

st: The Case of the Capricious Corpse
d: A young woman, attempting to rescue a charitable youth organization from predatory heirs, becomes involved in a murder.

st: The Case of the Playboy Pugilist
d: A wealthy sportsman teams up with a veteran boxing coach to train a young boxer, but the partnership ends with murder.

st: The Case of the Hateful Hero
d: Perry Mason defends a rookie policeman charged with both robbery and murder.

st: The Case of the Dodging Domino
d: Perry Mason defends a university professor accused of murdering a blackmailing songwriter.

st: The Case of the Double-Entry Mind
d: A mousy bookkeeper embezzles $201,000 from his company only to be thwarted by his boss' beautiful secretary.

st: The Case of the Unsuitable Uncle
d: Perry Mason's client, a seaman, doesn't have enough money to pay his lawyer's fees but makes a will with bequests of $300,000.

st: The Case of the Stand-In Sister
d: When an ex-mob kingpin flees a Senate hearing, he involves Perry Mason in a coast-to-coast search for evidence.

st: The Case of the Weary Watchdog
d: Perry Mason defends Della Street's socialite friend, Janet Brent, accused of murdering a blackmailer.

st: The Case of the Lurid Letter
d: Small-town prejudice erupts against a young high school teacher who is anonymously accused of improper behavior with her students.

st: The Case of the Fickle Filly
d: A man sets events toward his own murder when he jilts his sweetheart for an older woman, then buys the ex-girlfriend's prized racehorse.

st: The Case of the Polka-Dot Pony
d: A $200,000 trust fund may go to an airline hostess if Perry Mason can prove she is the baby who was left on an orphanage doorstep.

st: The Case of the Shoplifter's Shoe
d: The sister of a prominent jewel dealer is accused of both shoplifting and murder.
